items.summary: the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the capital early Saturday, and Saudi civil defence issued eight public emergency alerts in 24 hours. The coalition also struck the port of Hodeidah and military targets in Sanaa on Friday.
items.matters: the Houthis have threatened Jeddah and other Red Sea ports, the Al-Shuqaiq power station and Riyadh's financial centre, and the UN warns the fighting could disrupt aid routes in Yemen.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info A skyscraper housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund in Riyadh [File: AFP] By Al Jazeera Staff and AFP Published On 21 Nov 2026 21 Nov 2026 The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government said it has intercepted three ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels towards Riyadh, after a flurry of emergency alerts in the Saudi capital.

The attack early on Saturday morning came two days after a Houthi strike damaged the Public Investment Fund tower, the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper.

It was the third day in a row that Saudi Arabia issued and quickly lifted alerts for Riyadh.

Hours later, the coalition said that it destroyed another drone fired by the Houthis towards the kingdom’s south. It did not say which province was targeted.

Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency had issued eight public emergency alerts during a 24-hour period starting at 7:30am Saudi time (04:30 GMT) on Friday.

In Yemen, the Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Friday that it carried out a “special operation” against the Houthi-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah, as well as “military targets” in the capital, Sanaa.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said the strikes hit “operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles”, the AFP news agency reported.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has defended the coalition strikes on Hodeidah port, accusing the Houthis of using its facilities to receive smuggled Iranian weapons and conduct military operations.

The Houthis responded by threatening to attack Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports, warning airlines that Saudi Arabia’s airspace was “unsafe”.

They also threatened Riyadh’s financial centre and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq, in the southwest.

It warned that continued fighting could threaten vital supply routes for humanitarian aid in Yemen.

items.headline: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia for six months from 1 December
items.summary: the government blames Russia for an attempted arson attack on the drone maker Threod Systems, which the Kremlin denies. Moscow's Maria Zakharova called the move a "new Iron Curtain" and promised measures to protect Russia's interests.
items.matters: Estonia says the closure targets recruitment, influence operations, sabotage and sanctions evasion, and it will decide next year whether to extend it.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info An EU, Estonian and NATO flag flies near the bridge over the Narva River at the border crossing point with Russia in Narva, Estonia, on November 17, 2026 [Janis Laizans/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 20 Nov 2026 20 Nov 2026 Moscow has accused Estonia of planning to build a “new Iron Curtain”, and promised to respond, after the small Baltic nation formally decided to close all border crossings with Russia to the east and south.

Estonia’s government on Friday approved a preliminary six-month closure of its road border crossings from December 1, and will decide next year whether to extend it.

“Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East,” Zakharova added.

In Tallinn on Friday, Estonia’s Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna described the border closure as “an important measure”.

“It will reduce opportunities to exploit cross-border movement to recruit people, conduct influence operations, organise acts of sabotage or circumvent sanctions,” he said.

Estonia, a NATO and EU member and a staunch supporter of Ukraine, first announced the border closure earlier this month, accusing Russia of being behind an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.

The Kremlin denied the accusation at the time, saying it was part of what it called a pattern of false allegations levelled against Moscow by European countries.

Estonia’s northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations ⁠Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

Of the 760,000 people who crossed the Estonia-Russia border this year, 307,000 were Russian nationals, 175,000 were Estonian citizens and 54,000 held Finnish passports, Estonian ‌police ‌data showed.

Rail freight is not affected by the road closure, but remains subject to strict customs checks, Estonia said.

items.headline: Denmark expels Russia's defence attaché over an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian rapper
items.summary: Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen says the attaché must leave within seven days, and Danish intelligence suspects Russian intelligence planned the killing with the banned gang Loyal to Familia. Two Danish men are charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
items.matters: Copenhagen is also considering suspending Schengen visas for Russians, EU Council President Costa pledged EU backing, and Russia calls the expulsion "vengeful" and promises an "appropriate response".

“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attaché from Denmark” within seven days, Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Lokke Rasmussen told a news conference on Friday.

The expulsion ultimatum comes hours after Denmark’s intelligence agency, PET, said it suspected Russia of planning the assassination during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb with help of a Danish gang.

Danish public broadcaster DR named the rapper as Kyivstoner, who has both Ukrainian and US citizenship.

“The case shows, in our assessment, that the Russian intelligence services attempted to carry out an execution in Denmark,” he said.

According to PET, three people were stopped in a car near the music venue where the rapper was scheduled to perform on September 25. Police found firearms and knives in the vehicle.

items.headline: COP31 in Antalya runs into overtime with no deal on fossil fuels
items.summary: about 200 countries are split over a draft that no longer mentions fossil fuels after Saudi Arabia and other producers objected, and the text also dropped a $120bn adaptation-finance target. A third draft is expected Saturday.
items.matters: the EU warns the text "risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit", Panama and a dozen other countries threaten to walk away, and the US is absent for a second year.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info COP31's President and Turkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum speaks during a plenary session as part of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, on November 20, 2026 [Yasin Akgul/AFP] By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters Published On 20 Nov 2026 20 Nov 2026 The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels.

The two-week talks in Antalya, Turkiye, were due to end on Friday, when a late closing session approved some technical matters, but not the wider political deal.

“We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President and Turkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates.

Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference said the meeting lacked ambition to address the ‌worsening climate crisis and was on track to be the “worst COP ever”.

An opening draft from cohost and lead negotiator Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.

Oil producers have also resisted similar language at past talks, including at COP28 in 2023. The revised text also dropped a $120bn target for money to help poorer countries adapt to climate change.

The European Union said the draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. Panama, which signed a letter with a dozen other countries demanding “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”, threatened to walk away from the talks.

“It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels, and we simply will not put up with it,” Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, told a news conference.

The draft proposes raising the share of the world’s final energy consumption that comes from electricity to 35 percent by 2035. It does not say the power must come from renewables, and some countries want the target to say “clean”.

Some countries also reject a push to expand carbon capture, a technology that traps emissions from power plants and factories. They say it is costly and unproven, and could let polluters keep burning oil and gas.

“We want to see the references to false solutions removed,” said Vanuatu’s climate minister, Ralph Regenvanu.

items.headline: Rosyjskie obiekty spadły w trzech miejscach na Podkarpaciu i Lubelszczyźnie, NATO poderwało myśliwce
items.summary: w nocy z czwartku na piątek, podczas zmasowanego ataku na Ukrainę, w Mołodyczu, Rudniku nad Sanem i Nowym Lipowcu spadły dwie rakiety i prawdopodobnie dron odrzutowy, a szef MON Kosiniak-Kamysz mówi o prowokacji, nikt nie został ranny.
items.matters: wczoraj wojsko dopiero weryfikowało radary, dziś są potwierdzone miejsca upadku. Rutte rozmawiał z Tuskiem i nazwał incydent „wyraźnie niebezpiecznym", Tusk zapowiedział jego wizytę w Warszawie w sobotę, a MSZ wezwie rosyjskich przedstawicieli po „żelazne dowody" od wojska.
items.body:
Skomentuj Sekretarz generalny NATO Mark Rutte przekazał w piątek, że rozmawiał z szefem polskiego rządu Donaldem Tuskiem na temat „poważnych naruszeń” polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej. Będziemy nadal wzmacniać naszą zdolność do odstraszania i obrony - zaznaczył.

/ Kancelaria Prezesa Rady Ministrów W odpowiedzi na naruszenia polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej, do których doszło w nocy z czwartku na piątek, NATO poderwało myśliwce - przekazał Rutte we wpisie na platformie X.

„Rozmawiałem z premierem Donaldem Tuskiem o poważnych naruszeniach polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej minionej nocy. W odpowiedzi poderwano myśliwce NATO” - napisał dodając, że Sojusz będzie nadal „wzmacniać swoją zdolność do odstraszania i obrony”.

Jak dodał, incydent jest „wyraźnie niebezpieczny” i stanowi konsekwencję trwającej wojny Rosji przeciwko Ukrainie. Rutte potępił rosyjskie ataki oraz rozpętany przez Moskwę konflikt. Podkreślił również, że państwa NATO pozostają zjednoczone i będą nadal wspierać Ukrainę.

Podczas zmasowanych rosyjskich ataków na Ukrainę w nocy z czwartku na piątek doszło do naruszenia polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej.

Szef MON, wicepremier Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz przekazał, że obiekty spadły w trzech miejscach, są to: Mołodycz w powiecie jarosławskim, Rudnik nad Sanem w powiecie niżańskim oraz Nowy Lipowiec w powiecie biłgorajskim. W dwóch przypadkach jest obecnie mowa o rakiecie, w trzecim - najprawdopodobniej o dronie odrzutowym.

Premier Donald Tusk przekazał, że chodzi na pewno o obiekty rosyjskie. Szef rządu zapowiedział też, że w sobotę Rutte będzie w Warszawie, co da okazją do tego, by „poznać intencje dowództwa NATO po kolejnej rosyjskiej prowokacji”.

Kosiniak-Kamysz ogłosił z kolei, że będzie wnioskował do sekretarza generalnego NATO o wydzielenie dodatkowych sił i środków, by wzmocnić natowską misję Wschodnia Straż. Celem tej inicjatywy Sojuszu jest wsparcie obrony wschodniej flanki NATO, przede wszystkim w obszarze obrony powietrznej.

items.headline: Polska chce wzmocnienia Eastern Sentry, a wiceszef MON Tomczyk podpisał w USA umowę o testowaniu uzbrojenia
items.summary: po rozmowach w Pentagonie powiedział, że Amerykanie pytali, jakiej pomocy Polska potrzebuje najpierw, ale nie przedstawili swojej reakcji. Umowa, negocjowana 17 lat, umożliwia wspólną produkcję i testy systemów antydronowych oraz dostęp polskich naukowców do amerykańskich laboratoriów wojskowych.
items.matters: Tomczyk mówi, że Pentagon uważa kwestię amerykańskich baz w Polsce za „w zasadzie zamkniętą", ale decyzja należy do prezydenta USA i wymaga współpracy rządu z Nawrockim.
items.body:
Wiceminister obrony narodowej Cezary Tomczyk przekazał w Pentagonie szczegółowe informacje o wtargnięciu rosyjskich obiektów do polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej. Jak relacjonował, amerykańscy rozmówcy pytali, jakiego wsparcia Polska potrzebuje w pierwszej kolejności. Warszawa ma zwrócić się do wojsk USA w Europie oraz sekretarza generalnego NATO o wzmocnienie operacji „Eastern Sentry”.

Cezary Tomczyk rozmawiał w Pentagonie (fot. Pawel Wodzynski) / East News Rozmowy o wsparciu dla Polski Tomczyk spotkał się w Waszyngtonie z podsekretarzem obrony USA do spraw badań i inżynierii Emilem Michaelem. Powodem rozmów było podpisanie polsko-amerykańskiej umowy o współpracy w dziedzinie testowania uzbrojenia.

Wiceszef MON poinformował jednak, że przedstawił też informacje dotyczące rosyjskiego ataku na Ukrainę, który – jak ocenił – „pośrednio skończył się atakiem na Polskę”. Rozmawiał na ten temat również z podsekretarzem stanu do spraw bezpieczeństwa międzynarodowego Thomasem DiNanno.

Polska zwróci się do wojsk amerykańskich w Europie i do sekretarza generalnego NATO o wzmocnienie operacji „Eastern Sentry”, tak żeby kolejne siły i środki mogły zostać wydzielone w celu ochrony polskiego nieba – powiedział Tomczyk.

Nie chciał szerzej opisywać reakcji strony amerykańskiej. Zaznaczył, że rozmówcy uzgodnili, iż poczekają na oficjalne stanowisko władz USA, w tym prezydenta Donalda Trumpa.

Wiceminister ocenił, że naruszenie polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej było celową prowokacją. Zwrócił uwagę, że doszło do niego w czasie ćwiczeń wojskowych państw tzw. koalicji chętnych, w których uczestniczyli ministrowie obrony między innymi Wielkiej Brytanii i Francji.

Oczywiście będziemy wyjaśniać, na ile ten wlot był przypadkowy, ale chyba wszyscy mamy dość jasne poczucie, że ta koincydencja nie jest przypadkowa – mówił Tomczyk.

Jego zdaniem Rosja próbuje wywoływać chaos i podziały w zachodnich społeczeństwach, podważać zaufanie do armii oraz NATO, a także doprowadzić do ograniczenia pomocy dla Ukrainy.

Władimir Putin nie jest naszym przyjacielem, jest naszym zagrożeniem – podkreślił wiceszef MON, co można odczytywać jako nawiązanie do serdecznego powitania Trumpa i Putina na szczycie APEC.

Odnosząc się do pytań o to, dlaczego rosyjskie obiekty nie zostały zestrzelone, Tomczyk powołał się na ocenę wojska, według której nie było ku temu odpowiednich warunków.

Na pewno nie politycy powinni decydować o tym, kiedy są warunki do zestrzelenia – zaznaczył.

Zapewnił, że Polska ma zdolności do zwalczania rosyjskich rakiet i dronów. Przypomniał jednak, że nawet Ukraina, mimo…

items.headline: Zgromadzenie Ogólne TK zawiesiło prezesa Święczkowskiego i obniżyło mu pensję, a on twierdzi, że żadnego zgromadzenia nie było
items.summary: we wtorek sędziowie zgodzili się na pociągnięcie do odpowiedzialności karnej Święczkowskiego i wiceprezesa Sochańskiego, ale odmówili aresztowania prezesa, o które wnioskował prokurator generalny Żurek.
items.matters: TK wyjaśnił w piątek, że trzy równoległe obniżki o 50% dają łącznie 50%, a nie 150%. Spór o to, kto w ogóle kieruje Trybunałem, nakłada się na impas w rozmowach o TK w Kancelarii Prezydenta.
items.body:
Skomentuj Nie sumuje się obniżek wynagrodzenia wynikających z wykonywanych jednocześnie uchwał o uchyleniu immunitetu. Równoczesne obniżenie wynagrodzenia Bogdana Święczkowskiego w trzech uchwałach o 50 proc. oznacza obniżenie wynagrodzenia o połowę - przekazał Trybunał Konstytucyjny.

fot. Jacek Szydlowski / / FORUM Na stronie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego zamieszczono w piątek po południu komunikat uzupełniający dotyczący rozstrzygnięć w sprawie wniosków Prokuratora Generalnego o uchylenie immunitetu sędziom TK.

Wskazano w nim m.in., że przepis ustawy o statusie sędziów TK „reguluje w szczególny sposób kwestię kworum wskazując, że wyrażenie zgody na pociągnięcie sędziego do odpowiedzialności karnej następuje bezwzględną większością głosów sędziów Trybunału uczestniczących w Zgromadzeniu Ogólnym”. „Do podjęcia uchwały nie jest zatem wymagane kworum” - podkreślono.

Jak dodano w komunikacie udzielone zgody na uchylenie immunitetu „dotyczą przestępstw umyślnych ściganych z oskarżenia publicznego”. „Zgromadzenie miało zatem obowiązek rozstrzygnąć z urzędu, w tych samych uchwałach, o zawieszeniu sędziów w czynnościach służbowych oraz o obniżeniu ich wynagrodzeń na czas zawieszenia” - czytamy.

„Każda z trzech uchwał dotyczących Bogdana Święczkowskiego obejmuje zawieszenie w czynnościach służbowych i obniżenie wynagrodzenia związane z odrębną sprawą. Ustanie zawieszenia w jednej sprawie samo przez się nie powoduje ustania zawieszenia w pozostałych” - wyjaśniono w komunikacie.

Jednocześnie zaznaczono, że „obniżek wynagrodzenia wynikających z uchwał wykonywanych jednocześnie za ten sam okres nie sumuje się”. „Stosuje się najwyższy poziom obniżenia określony w tych uchwałach. Równoczesne wykonywanie trzech uchwał przewidujących obniżenie wynagrodzenia Święczkowskiego o 50 proc. oznacza zatem obniżenie jego wynagrodzenia o 50 proc.” - wskazano.

We wtorek Zgromadzenie Ogólne Sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego zwołane przez sędzię Annę Korwin-Piotrowską zajmowało się wnioskami szefa MS, prokuratora generalnego Waldemara Żurka o uchylenie immunitetów prezesowi TK Bogdanowi Święczkowskiemu i wiceprezesowi Trybunału Bartłomiejowi Sochańskiemu.

Zgromadzenie podjęło we wtorek łącznie cztery uchwały „o zezwoleniu na pociągnięcie do odpowiedzialności karnej sędziów TK Święczkowskiego oraz Sochańskiego”.

items.headline: Komisja Europejska częściowo zatwierdziła ostatni wniosek Polski o płatność z KPO na 12,7 mld euro
items.summary: spełniono 76 z 77 kamieni milowych, a niespełniony dotyczy modernizacji portów obsługujących morskie farmy wiatrowe.
items.matters: kwota może zostać proporcjonalnie obniżona po odpowiedzi Polski, ale w grudniu spodziewany jest przelew około 55 mld zł (29,8 mld zł dotacji i 25,9 mld zł pożyczek), jeśli Komitet Ekonomiczno-Finansowy wyda pozytywną opinię.
items.body:
Skomentuj Komisja Europejska częściowo pozytywnie oceniła ostatni polski wniosek o wypłatę z KPO, opiewający na 12,7 mld euro - poinformowała KE. Bruksela stwierdziła, że jeden z 77 wskaźników nie został w pełni zrealizowany. Jeśli KE potwierdzi swoją ocenę, kwota płatności dla Polski może zostać odpowiednio zmniejszona.

fot. RaffMaster / / Shutterstock "Komisja Europejska częściowo zatwierdziła szósty i ostatni wniosek Polski o wypłatę kwoty 12,7 mld euro w ramach Instrumentu Odbudowy i Odporności (RRF)" - napisała KE w komunikacie.

Bruksela stwierdziła, że Polska w zadowalającym stopniu zrealizowała 76 z 77 etapów i celów określonych w decyzji wykonawczej Rady.

items.headline: PGZ podpisała z Saabem licencję na produkcję w Polsce amunicji moździerzowej 60,7 mm
items.summary: Dezamet będzie wytwarzać amunicję MAPAM z pociskiem odłamkowym, zaprojektowaną do moździerza „Szerszeń" z Zakładów Mechanicznych Tarnów.
items.matters: umowa wynika z programu ORKA, w którym Saab zbuduje trzy okręty podwodne A26, ale nie ujawniono wolumenów, wartości ani terminów dostaw.
items.body:
Skomentuj Zakłady Metalowe Dezamet, spółka Polskiej Grupy Zbrojeniowej, podpisały ze szwedzkim koncernem Saab umowę licencyjną na produkcję i sprzedaż w Polsce amunicji moździerzowej MAPAM kalibru 60,7 mm - poinformowały w piątek PGZ i Agencja Uzbrojenia.

/ PGZ O podpisaniu umowy PGZ i Agencja Uzbrojenia poinformowały we wpisach na platformie X. Projekt zakłada wdrożenie do produkcji naboju moździerzowego z pociskiem odłamkowym, zgodnego ze standardami NATO. Amunicja ma być używana w moździerzu „Szerszeń” produkowanym przez Zakłady Mechaniczne Tarnów.

Agencja Uzbrojenia wskazała, że umowa jest efektem realizacji programu ORKA i kontraktów wynegocjowanych przez jej zespół.

Jak podała PGZ, umowa oznacza transfer technologii, rozwój kompetencji inżynieryjnych i produkcyjnych oraz wzmocnienie krajowego łańcucha dostaw dla sektora obronnego. Grupa oceniła, że produkcja amunicji w Polsce zwiększy bezpieczeństwo dostaw dla Sił Zbrojnych RP i wzmocni potencjał przemysłowy wschodniej flanki NATO.

- Współpraca pomiędzy PGZ i Saab jest przykładem nowoczesnego partnerstwa przemysłowego, w którym kluczową rolę odgrywa rozwój kompetencji, transfer wiedzy oraz budowanie krajowych zdolności. Dzisiejsza umowa jest naturalnym etapem konsekwentnego współdziałania - podkreślił cytowany we wpisie wiceprezes PGZ Piotr Zawieja.

MAPAM (Mortar Anti-Personnel Anti-Materiel) to rodzaj amunicji moździerzowej o zwiększonej skuteczności rażenia odłamkami, opracowany przez szwajcarską spółkę Saab Bofors Dynamics Switzerland.

Konstrukcja pocisku MAPAM opiera się na zastosowaniu korpusu zawierającego tysiące prefabrykowanych odłamków, najczęściej w postaci kulek wolframowych lub stalowych, zatopionych w matrycy z tworzywa sztucznego lub metalu. Dzięki temu po detonacji pocisk generuje kontrolowane i gęste pole rażenia, znacznie skuteczniejsze od tradycyjnej amunicji żeliwnej czy stalowej.

Amunicja ta jest produkowana w kilku standardowych kalibrach NATO, w tym 60 mm (dokładnie 60,7 mm) oraz 81 mm. Naboje wyposażone są w nowoczesne zapalniki, umożliwiające m.in. detonację zbliżeniową nad celem, co dodatkowo zwiększa pole rażenia przy zwalczaniu celów ukrytych w okopach lub za przeszkodami terenowymi.

items.headline: Wall Street has its worst week since the pandemic
items.summary: the S&P 500 lost 8.6% on the week, its steepest drop since the 2 April 2025 tariff shock. The Dow fell about 8%, its worst since March 2020, and the Nasdaq-100 fell 10%. The Nasdaq Composite was down almost 4% on Friday afternoon, wiping out all of its 2026 gains.
items.matters: the S&P 500 and Dow both entered correction territory, and the semiconductor index fell more than 10% on Friday alone. That is a deeper rout than yesterday's 2.25% Nasdaq fall.
items.body:
Piątkowa sesja zakończyła wyjątkowo trudny tydzień na Wall Street. Najmocniej przeceniane były akcje spółek półprzewodnikowych i firm związanych ze sztuczną inteligencją, w tym Nvidii. Indeks branży półprzewodników SOX stracił w piątek ponad 10 proc.

Zdj. ilustracyjne / Shutterstock Jak podaje CNBC, indeks Dow Jones spadł w skali tygodnia o 8 proc. Był to jego najsłabszy wynik od marca 2020 roku, czyli początku pandemii Covid-19.

Nasdaq-100 stracił 10 proc., również najwięcej od okresu pandemii. Indeks S&P 500 obniżył się o 8,6 proc. – najmocniej od gwałtownej reakcji rynków po ogłoszeniu przez Donalda Trumpa globalnych ceł 2 kwietnia ubiegłego roku.

Szczególnie silna była przecena firm produkujących układy scalone. Indeks SOX, skupiający największe spółki z branży półprzewodników, obniżył się tylko w piątek o ponad 10 proc. Według Bloomberga był to dla niego najgorszy tydzień od 2001 roku.

Spadki koncentrowały się w sektorze technologicznym, zwłaszcza wśród firm korzystających z boomu na sztuczną inteligencję. Jednocześnie relatywnie lepiej radziły sobie m.in. sieci supermarketów oraz spółki odzieżowe.

Piąty dzień z rzędu taniały akcje Nvidii. Od październikowego szczytu ich kurs stracił już ponad 40 proc. wartości.

Przecena nastąpiła mimo opublikowania przez spółkę rekordowych wyników kwartalnych pod względem przychodów i zysków. Nastroje inwestorów pogorszyły jednak doniesienia Reutersa, według których amerykańska Komisja Papierów Wartościowych i Giełd (SEC) bada praktyki księgowe firmy. Informacje te oparto na źródłach agencji – postępowanie nie przesądza o stwierdzeniu naruszeń.

Wyraźnie tracił również AMD. Na kurs spółki wpłynęły doniesienia, że jej procesory mogły trafiać do chińskich firm objętych amerykańskimi sankcjami.

Sytuacji w sektorze nie poprawił giełdowy debiut laboratorium sztucznej inteligencji Anthropic. Dzień po pierwszym notowaniu akcje spółki spadły o 8,5 proc., po tym jak w czwartek zyskały 17 proc.

„Wall Street Journal” ocenił, że zakłady inwestorów na rozwój sztucznej inteligencji zaczynają się chwiać. CNBC wskazuje z kolei na ryzyko załamania się rynku.

Wśród czynników wymienianych przez stację są sygnały możliwego hamowania wydatków na infrastrukturę AI, perspektywa zaostrzenia regulacji sektora technologicznego oraz problemy wokół Nvidii.

items.headline: An AI claims a solution to the Riemann hypothesis, and a human claims one too
items.summary: Levent Alpöge says he found a Lean-compilable proof with Claude, and mathematicians in a Zulip chat, including MIT's Andrew Sutherland, report that the code compiles. Stanford's Alessandro Masullo separately posted an entirely human-authored proof of the General Riemann hypothesis after 12 years of work.
items.matters: independent sources have checked the Lean proof, but nobody has yet explained the argument in human-readable form, and Masullo's draft is not in Lean, so neither claim is settled.
items.body:
AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too Tim Fernholz 11:32 AM PST · November 20, 2026 It’s a big week for Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics.

“The precise timing is horrible,” he wrote in an essay announcing his findings and describing how he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to announce that he had found a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis, which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems.

The hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers. If the claimed result holds true, we’re entering sublime-mysteries-of-the-universe territory.

The cohomology bound is proved by what looks like an automorphy-lifting argument. It genuinely uses the existence of Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM fields, along with base change, Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel’s purity, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, the main theorem of CM, Deligne–Ribet and more.

For my part, I tapped out of mathematics at college calculus, so I can’t help decode exactly what that means.

It will be a while before the mathematics community feels like it has a handle on the proof, but most appear confident that the formalized Lean result will hold. Lean is an an open-source coding language used to express mathematical ideas as code, allowing proofs to be formally verified. Several participants in the Zulip chat, including MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland, say they have successfully confirmed that Alpöge’s solution can be compiled successfully.

Alpöge appeared in his essay to feel a bit guilty about releasing the proof without a truly human-intelligible explanation, but his obsession with the problem since childhood made him feel he “could not live” if he waited to release the finding.

However, for all that action to mean anything, we’ll have to wait for humans to be able to understand the result and explain it to each other, something Alpöge has committed to pursue.

Alpöge and a collaborator, NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, also released another important proof related to the Navier-Stokes equations, problems that helped kick off the race between frontier labs and mathematicians to solve outstanding problems this summer.

Without being expressed in Lean, it is too early to say whether the proof checks…

items.matters: Nvidia posted $115.8bn quarterly revenue, up 103%, on 17 November, so the business looks unaffected for now, but investor confidence has dipped and the H200 export permission is under scrutiny.
items.body:
The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline Amanda Silberling 12:18 PM PST · November 19, 2026 Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

Nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress said that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t…

items.headline: Amazon says China-linked attackers used autonomous AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day
items.summary: the open-source Cairn framework found a path-traversal flaw in the MONAI Label medical imaging app, and about 11 minutes after mapping the API the agents could write files on the server. The campaign hit East Asian universities over 48 hours from 8 September.
items.matters: Bell Canada also confirmed an "agentic" attacker breached its Maximo pre-production system on 17 November, and Gambit Security links a Chinese operator using Cairn to at least 27 compromised companies.
items.body:
Suspected Chinese spies deployed AI agents which worked autonomously to find a zero-day in an open source application and then abuse the flaw to break into university networks, gaining full control of a server, according to Amazon CISO CJ Moses.

The China-linked attacker used Cairn, an open source, penetration-testing framework that has become increasingly popular with cybercriminals who use the AI tool to carry out multi-stage intrusions with no human assistance.

In this case, the agents found and exploited a zero-day MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application. Amazon notified the project's maintainers of the vulnerability, and they released a fix and a security advisory.

On September 10, Amazon's Threat Intelligence Team found a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn that provided visibility into the campaign targeting universities in East Asia, outside Mainland China, Moses said in a Friday report shared with The Register.

The campaign occurred over a period of 48 hours beginning on September 8, and the prompts were written in Simplified Chinese, with timestamps in executed scripts configured to China Standard Time.

Before the AI agents found and exploited the zero day, however, they tried to break into another university’s Redis server over about 16 hours and 148 sequential actions, including abusing Redis's replication feature to load unauthorized code, escaping its scripting sandbox, writing to its configuration files, and corrupting its memory.

None of these were successful, and when those actions failed, the agents also attempted a Log4Shell injection against a different service, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack against a vulnerability in a co-located Qdrant instance, and several credential sprays against PostgreSQL, SSH, and other tools.

Meanwhile, a separate operation running for more than 6 hours targeted a university GPU server with another credential-spray attack, compiling a list of 80 real user names found across the school’s public websites, academic papers and other documents.

"Neither operation succeeded, yet together they show that the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction," Moses wrote.

Then the AI agents found the zero-day path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label, and this time they were able to gain access to the server.

items.headline: VMware's vCenter flaw was exploited as a zero-day since September
items.summary: Mandiant attributes it to Armory Castle, formerly UNC5221, a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group. The authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 gives a session as administrator@vsphere.local, and Broadcom fixed it on 19 November in VMSA-2026-0009.
items.matters: yesterday's advisory read as a routine patch, but attackers have had the hole for about two and a half months, Broadcom offers no workaround, and it is part of an intrusion that began with a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day.
items.body:
Broadcom has released security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server, a management platform organizations use to manage VMware virtualized environments.

According Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a vulnerable vCenter Server to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.

Successful exploitation can allow attackers to obtain administrative access to vCenter, giving them control over the virtual machines managed by the server.

Broadcom patched the vulnerability on November 19 in VMSA-2026-0009, which also fixes four other vulnerabilities affecting VMware SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows.

"You are affected if you are running any version of VMware vCenter, SDDC Manager, or VMware Tools for Windows prior to the versions listed as "fixed" in the VMSA," Broadcom's security advisory reads.

"This includes vCenter and SDDC Manager deployed standalone and as part of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Telco Cloud Platform, and VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure, as well as VMware Tools installed in Windows virtual machines."

The company considers the vCenter vulnerability as an emergency update, urging organizations to install the patches as soon as possible.

Broadcom says there are no official workarounds for the vulnerabilities, although network restrictions and firewall controls can help reduce exposure.

While Broadcom has not confirmed that the flaw was exploited, researchers at Google's Mandiant have documented attacks exploiting CVE-2026-123890.

In a report published today, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) revealed that a suspected Chinese state-sponsored hacking group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-123890 in early September 2026.

"Successful exploitation results in a remote authentication bypass which creates an authenticated session established as administrator@vsphere.local," explains Mandiant.

"Using the authenticated administrator session, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands and acquire files, including the data.mdb database, by leveraging the vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC interface vmdirdbcp."

Armory Castle is a cyberespionage group known for exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in enterprise network appliances, including Citrix NetScaler and Ivanti Connect…

items.headline: UK tribunal forces the government to admit it served Apple a secret encryption-access notice
items.summary: the Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's argument that even acknowledging the notice would harm national security. The judgment does not disclose what the notice demands.
items.matters: Apple filed a second challenge in July, a substantive hearing is expected in the first half of 2027, and Liberty and Privacy International are separately challenging the notice regime.
items.body:
The Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN), rejecting the Home Office's argument that acknowledging its existence would damage national security.

The three judges pointed to extensive public reporting, statements by US officials, and media briefings they concluded had been authorized by the UK government.

The Home Office had previously adopted its "neither confirm nor deny" (NCND) policy, as is standard when discussing national security matters.

The story broke in February 2025, when The Washington Post reported that the Home Office had demanded an iCloud backdoor the previous month.

A TCN is a notice issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, which compels recipients, such as tech companies, to implement technical changes that facilitate the UK government's legal surveillance powers.

For Apple, a company that has long made privacy central to its marketing, and famously rejected an FBI order to break open an iPhone to assist a terror probe, being served the TCN meant it either had to somehow defy a legal order issued by the UK, or undermine the encryption technology that customers expected.

items.summary: C# 15 brings union types, closed hierarchies and extension indexers, and the libraries gain Zstandard compression and System.Text.Json union support.
items.matters: .NET 10 remains the LTS option Dalamud runs on, so this is a heads-up rather than an upgrade, and the post lists no specific breaking changes and points to the breaking-changes docs.
items.body:
Today, we’re excited to announce the release of.NET 11! This year’s release makes building modern applications faster, more productive, and has improvements across C# 15, ASP.NET Core,.NET MAUI, and Windows development. With hundreds of runtime optimizations, more responsive SDK tooling, and less overhead in everyday commands, you can spend less time waiting and more time creating. Build richer web and cross-platform applications, take advantage of new C# language features, and explore AI-powered development with improved tools and agentic capabilities.

Explore.NET 11 with the product teams and community at.NET Conf 2026. The conference includes product team sessions on November 10 and 11, followed by two days of community sessions.

The what’s new in.NET 11 overview links to the full details. Here are the changes behind those headlines and how to start using them.

C# 15 is the default language version for projects targeting.NET 11. Union types are one of its biggest additions: a value can be one of a declared set of case types, with conversions from those types and exhaustiveness checking in switch expressions.

Consider a product lookup that either finds a product or reports that it wasn’t found:

ProductLookup result = new Product(42, "Mechanical keyboard"); string message = result switch { Product product => $"Found {product.Name}", ProductNotFound missing => $"No product with ID {missing.Id}", }; Console.WriteLine(message); public sealed record Product(int Id, string Name); public sealed record ProductNotFound(int Id); public union ProductLookup(Product, ProductNotFound); The result type tells a caller which outcomes it needs to handle. There’s no need to use object or an unrelated base class just to put those outcomes behind one return type.

C# 15 also adds closed hierarchies. A closed class limits direct derivation to its declaring assembly, giving the compiler the information it needs to check patterns over the hierarchy. Unions are useful when you want to combine existing types; closed hierarchies fit models where you own the inheritance relationship.

Smaller language features help with everyday code, too. Collection expression arguments let you pass constructor or factory arguments without giving up collection expression syntax:

HashSet<string> names = [with(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase), "Alice", "ALICE", "Bob"]; Console.WriteLine(names.Count); This prints 2: the comparer controls equality, so "Alice" and "ALICE" are one entry.

items.headline: Blizzard says spellpower gear is falling behind and healers are hard to field
items.summary: on the WoW Forever Podcast, Principal Designer Kris Zierhut said more spellpower items are coming in future patches, and Aidan Moon (Zirene) said the team is looking at making healing less inconvenient.
items.matters: yesterday's Episode 8 entry gave only the title, and the content is now confirmed, but no immediate fix was promised.
items.body:
The very first topics covered in the latest episode of the WoW Forever Podcast are regarding casters and healers, who players feel have recieved the short end of the stick while leveling so far.

Principal Designer Kris Zierhut stated that the developers are aware that spellpower gear isn’t currently keeping up with gear for physical damage dealers, and they have plans to add more in future patches to make caster specializations more competitive while leveling.

A tougher problem to solve is the lack of healers for dungeons. Senior Game Designer Aidan Moon, AKA Zirene, acknowledged the difficulty in needing to have a dedicated healing spec and set, particularly for higher level dungeons, while also maintaining a damage setup for questing. No immediate solution was promised, but the developers are weighing options to further incentivize people to play healers, or at least make it less inconvenient to do so.

items.headline: A designer says he wants to "get rid of BiS" in Forever raid itemization
items.summary: Aidan Moon wants more items with unique effects against certain creature types or biomes, so players may need different gear for each boss.
items.matters: players will carry far more items, so the team plans bigger bags and better inventory sorting.
items.body:
Following a general discussion of flavor items in WoW Forever in this week’s episode of the WoW Forever Podcast, Senior Game Designer Aidan Moon, AKA Zirene, went on to talk about how the developers are approaching endgame gearing. He said their goal is to make itemization more interesting and complex so players aren’t encouraged to chase down an exact best-in-slot item for each slot and ignore everything else.

One way they’re trying to change that is by adding more items that have unique effects against certain types of creatures or in certain biomes. Raids will often have different biomes in different parts of the instance as well as different types of bosses. Ultimately, players may be prioritizing completely different gear for each boss if they want to truly min/max.

Obviously this means that players will be carrying a lot more items around, but the developers are planning to expand bags to account for that and generally improve inventory and item sorting.

items.headline: Glastonbury 2027 announces Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish as Pyramid Stage headliners
items.summary: Cher takes the Sunday legends slot at the 23–27 June festival, and Styles, Cher and Kraftwerk all make their Glastonbury debuts.
items.matters: the Guardian, as relayed by Stereogum, calls them the youngest headliners of the 21st century, and tickets sold out before the line-up was announced.
items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google There was no Glastonbury Festival in 2026. Every few years, the massive English music festival takes a year off so that the soil at Worthy Farm, the festival site, can recover. Today, however, the Glastonbury bookers have announced the initial lineup for the 2027 festival. This time around, the three big Pyramid Stage headliners are Sam Fender, Harry Styles, and Billie Eilish, while Cher will play in the Sunday afternoon "legends" slot.

As The Guardian notes, this is the youngest set of Glastonbury headliners of the 21st century. Fender and Styles are both 32, and Eilish is 24. Both Eilish and Fender have played Glastonbury before — the two of them went back-to-back to close out the Pyramid Stage in 2022 — but Styles and Cher will make their Glastonbury debuts. Kraftwerk, another legendary act, will also play Glasto for the first time, as will younger acts like Angine de Poitrine, Sombr, Adéla, the Womack Sisters, and Sienna Spiro.

Even without the full festival lineup being announced yet, the bill is already predictably huge. The other acts booked to play include (deep breath) Massive Attack, Crowded House, Primal Scream, Saint Etienne, the xx, FKA twigs, Kacey Musgraves, Robyn, Lily Allen, the War On Drugs, King Gizzard And The Lizard Wizard, the Streets, Underworld, Texas, Ellie Goulding, Little Simz, Lola Young, FLO, Christine And The Queens, Young Fathers, the Avalanches, Basement Jaxx, Nia Archives, Hot Chip, De La Soul, Mike D 5D, Chvrches, Blood Orange, Thundercat, Dinosaur Jr., Westside Cowboy, Underscores, Chase & Status, Confidence Man, Ezra Collective, Leon Bridges, Tinariwen, Lianna La Havas, Florence Road, Getdown Services, Thee Sacred Souls, Atarashi Gakko!, Nao, and Ecca Vandal.

The festival goes down 6/23-27 at Worthy Farm in Pilton. Tickets already went up on sale and sold out before the lineup was announced. For all the relevant info, check over here.

items.headline: Ella Langley wins six CMA Awards in one night, a record
items.summary: she took Entertainer, Album and Song of the Year, and "Choosin' Texas" also won Single of the Year, beating Taylor Swift's "I Knew It, I Knew You".
items.matters: the previous record was five, shared by Johnny Cash, Vince Gill, Alan Jackson and Lainey Wilson, and Swift returned to the CMAs for the first time in 13 years.
items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google Cindy Ord/Getty Images When Taylor Swift released her Toy Story 5 soundtrack song " I Knew It, I Knew You " earlier this year, it was explicitly marketed as Swift's return to country music, the genre where she began her career. That track's actual country qualities are debatable, but they were enough to get Swift back onstage at the Country Music Association awards for the first time in many years.

The CMAs are country music's biggest annual awards show, and Swift used to be a regular there. This year's awards show went down on Wednesday night, and Swift gave her first CMAs performance in 13 years. (She also presented an award in 2016, so this was her first time back on the show in any capacity in a decade.) Swift performed "I Knew It, I Knew You," and she also worked in one chorus of her early smash "Our Song,." which just turned 20. Beyond that, she made sure that her performance had all sorts of nods to her past and to country music in general.

Naturally, Swift's performance was an elaborate production. She started it off in a dressing room full of her old costumes. As she wound her way through the backstage hallways at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena, lots of country stars made cameos: Brad Paisley, Little Big Town, Sugarland, Brooks & Dunn, Lainey Wiilson, Eric Church. When she came out onto a stage made to look like the tree from Toy Story 5, her onetime tourmate Keith Urban joined her on banjo. There are already TikToks breaking down all the references in the performance, which you can watch below.

Swift also presented the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award to Brook & Dunn, who got a tribute performance from Halestorm, Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, HARDY, and Marcus King and won Vocal Duo Of The Year for the 17th time. "I Knew It, I Knew You" won a Hollywood Music In Media Award, and Swift accepted that one in a pre-recorded video.

But Taylor Swift wasn't the night's big winner. Instead, that distinction went to Ella Langley, the latest singer to break out of country music and dominate the pop charts. Langley set a new record for most CMA. Langley won six awards, including Entertainer, Album, and Song Of The Year. One of the people who Langley defeated was Taylor Swift, as her record-setting smash "Choosin' Texas" beat "I Knew It, I Knew You" for Single Of The Year.

items.headline: Tame Impala breaks the record for most ARIA Awards of all time
items.summary: Stereogum reported the milestone on 18 November.
items.matters: it is a record for the Australian industry's main awards, set by the act's latest run of wins.
items.body:
This one checks out. When you think of successful Australian musicians, Tame Impala has to be near the top of your list. As of today, one list he definitely tops is the list of most ARIA Awards, the top music industry honor in Australia.

This year's ARIA Awards took place earlier today at Hordern Pavilion in Sydney. Kevin Parker's project totaled seven awards for 2026: Album Of The Year (for Deadbeat), Best Solo Artist, Best Pop Release (for "Dracula"), Song Of The Year (for "Dracula"), Best Engineered Release (for Deadbeat), Best Produced Release (for Deadbeat), and the Global Impact Award, presented by Savage Garden's Darren Hayes. This brings Parker's career total to 22 ARIA wins, breaking a record previously held by Silverchair and John Farnham.

"Hopefully this can once and for all, everyone can accept and realize and not need to joke about it that Tame Impala is in fact just one guy," Parker said from the stage.

Over in America, this week Tame's Jennie collaboration "Dracula" holds at its #3 peak on the Hot 100 — the highest charting song ever for either artist. Next year, Parker will compete for four Grammys, including Record Of The Year, and headline Coachella.

Moments later, a red-haired woman fell to her death outside the Arconia and was revealed to be Cinda herself.

In a previous interview with TVLine, series co-creator John Hoffman described Cinda as "a real touchstone" for the trio, explaining that following her trail to London means "stepping in the footsteps of someone who died," while also giving Charles, Oliver, and Mabel an opportunity to see themselves in a new light.

items.headline: 3 Body Problem season 2 gets a teaser and a 14 January 2027 date
items.summary: Netflix's six one-hour episodes open with the San-Ti writing "We are here" in the sky.
items.matters: the teaser says they have sent an emissary to end the conflict.
items.body:
On Tuesday, Netflix released the first trailer for the sci-fi drama's upcoming second season. And in it, the alien race that's determined to take over Earth makes its presence known in a big way: By writing "We are here" in the sky.

But let's back up a minute. The series is based on Liu Cixin's Remembrance of Earth's Past novels; the first season, which began streaming in 2024, chronicled how a mysterious virtual reality video game was tied to the extraterrestrials' plan for a global takeover. In the Season 1 finale, scientists tried — and failed — to interact with the aliens, and the United Nations moved to stop the oncoming attack.

"We haven't spoken with you for a long time, but we've been watching," the aliens, who are known as the San-Ti, inform Earth in the video above. "War would be devastating for both our peoples. So we have sent an emissary to meet you in hopes of ending our conflict."

Courtesy of Netflix Netflix will release "3 Body Problem" Season 2 on Thursday, January 14, 2027. The season will consist of six one-hour episodes.

The Season 2 cast includes Jess Hong (Sky's "Inked"), Jovan Adepo ("IT: Welcome to Derry"), Eiza González ("From Dusk Till Dawn: The Series"), Benedict Wong ("Marco Polo"), Liam Cunningham ("Game of Thrones"), Marlo Kelly (Australia's "Home and Away"), Saamer Usmani ("Inventing Anna"), Sea Shimooka ("Arrow"), Claudia Doumit ("The Boys"), and Ellie De Lange ("Wolf Hall").

In addition, the guest-star roster includes Alfie Allen ("Game of Thrones"), David Yip ("Pennyworth"), Jordan Sunshine ("The Pitt"), and Josh Brener ("Stuart Fails to Save the Universe").

Miguel Sapochnik and Jeremy Podeswa, both of whom directed multiple "Game of Thrones" episodes, will helm three episodes each in the upcoming "3 Body Problem" season. The series was co-created by "Thrones" bosses David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and Alexander Woo.

items.headline: Slow Horses is renewed for seasons 9 and 10
items.summary: Apple TV made the order less than a month after the season 6 finale on 21 October.
items.matters: season 7 ("Bad Actors") is already finished and due in 2027, and season 8 ("Clown Town") is in production for 2028.
items.body:
Apple TV Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Slow Horses" isn't going anywhere anytime soon: Apple TV has renewed the Emmy- and BAFTA-winning drama for Seasons 9 and 10 — meaning fans can anticipate at least four more seasons of the Gary Oldman spy thriller.

The double renewal comes less than a month after the Season 6 finale, which dropped October 21. The first six seasons are currently available to stream, while Season 7, which will adapt Mick Herron's eighth "Slough House" novel, "Bad Actors," and Season 8, based on the ninth novel, "Clown Town," had already been ordered.

"Slow Horses," which first aired in 2022, is described as "a darkly humorous espionage drama that follows a dysfunctional team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 known un-affectionately as Slough House. Oldman stars as Jackson Lamb, the brilliant but cantankerous leader of the spies, who end up in Slough House due to their career-ending mistakes and who frequently find themselves blundering around the smoke and mirrors of the espionage world."

Seasons 1 and 2, which adapted "Slow Horses" and "Dead Lions," premiered in April and December of that year. Those were followed by an annual fall release cadence, with Seasons 3 through 6 (which adapted "Real Tigers," "Spook Street," "London Rules" and, in Season 6, both "Joe Country" and "Slough House") released between 2023 and 2026.

Season 7 is already in the can, and expected in 2027, while Season 8 is currently in production for an anticipated 2028 release.

The early renewal for Seasons 9 and 10 arrives just one day after series star Olivia Cooke suggested that Season 8 would mark the end of the road for the acclaimed series. But the double renewal does raise an interesting question: With the show set to exhaust all nine of Herron's currently published novels by the end of Season 8, what stories will Seasons 9 and 10 tell? Apple has not yet specified.

Brad Bird channels classic Hollywood in ‘Ray Gunn’, bringing a sprawling retrofuturistic mystery to Netflix.

Picture Credit: Netflix Ray Gunn has lived in animation legend Brad Bird’s mind rent-free, predating that of his iconic features Iron Giant, The Incredibles, and the Australian breakdancer of the same name. His long-gestating passion project about a private detective operating in a retrofuturistic alien realm has finally been realized, and the result is a fun, mesmerizing film noir that acts as a love letter to classic cinema and a sophisticated gateway for families to introduce their kids to the genre that has been untapped in animation since Roger Rabbit. It really feels as if Brad Bird created his own Blade Runner for kids not old enough to watch Blade Runner.

In the retrofuturistic city of Metropia, where flying cars and AI-surveilled ads are plentiful, aliens are seen as second-class citizens in a human-prioritized society. While most humans are discriminatory, Raymond “Ray” Gunn (Sam Rockwell) isn’t. An ex-cop turned freelance P.I., Gunn struggles to keep his business afloat while operating in a grimy, corrupt underbelly. His insistence on always doing the right thing causes his finances to decline—he can’t pay his longtime cyclopsian, tripod-legged work partner, Eye-Ra Kadok (Tom Waits), and he’s fending off repos from taking his office’s possessions. All that luck turns when he’s hired by Arnold Dom (Bobby Cannavale), the fourth husband of Venus Nova (Scarlett Johansson)—a charming yet volatile Britney Spears-meets-Taylor-Swift-esque megastar songstress—to follow her when he suspects unfaithfulness. His better judgment on the assignment leads her label company, Megamax, CEO Barry (Alan Tudyk) to hire Ray as her bodyguard to keep the star out of trouble as they’re antsy over another public scandal amid her latest album release. As folks in Nova’s orbit are murdered, Gunn and Kadok are thrust into a vast web of mysteries involving alien crime bosses, finicky particle guns, an unsuspecting romance between a starlet and a detective, and a secret that could turn all of Metropia upside down.

Ray Gunn is Brad Bird in his maximalist cinephile mode, wearing his love for Golden Age Hollywood noir flicks on his sleeve and demonstrating classic noir prowess with the same patience and visual style as the films he’s tributing. Much like his prior works, he immerses you in his classic-noir science-fiction realm, elaborating on Gunn’s lack of depth as his morally upright backbone contrasts with the gritty environment. Animation be damned, we haven’t…

items.headline: Commission opens consultation on the AI Act fundamental rights impact assessment template (16 November)
items.summary: the draft template for deployers of high-risk AI systems under Article 27 was opened for feedback on 16 November, and the consultation closes on 15 January 2027.
items.matters: if you build or deploy high-risk systems, the questionnaire shows what customers will need from you, and the full template contents were behind a sign-in, so read the Commission's consultation page before commenting.

items.headline: Commission seeks input on DSA guidelines for advertising repositories (4 November)
items.summary: the call for evidence covers the design of the ad libraries that very large platforms and search engines must keep under Article 39, including searchability, targeting insights and accessibility. It closes on 2 December 2026, a targeted public consultation follows in 2027, and final guidelines are planned for Q2 2028.
items.matters: it applies to VLOP and VLOSE providers, so anyone building ad-library APIs or tooling that uses them has a window to shape the design now.

items.headline: Eight member states launch the EDU-EDIC digital sovereignty consortium for education (20 November)
items.summary: Belgium, Croatia, Finland, France, Greece, Slovenia, Spain and the Netherlands, which hosts it, will pool resources for shared, interoperable infrastructure covering cloud, AI for education and secure data exchange between institutions.
items.matters: it is a public-sector buyer pushing sovereign, interoperable infrastructure, which affects EdTech vendors selling into these countries, though the page gives no funding figures.

items.headline: Aeon on Irish selkie folklore
items.summary: Jordan Lee Borgman's essay runs about 3,700 words (roughly 15 minutes) and argues that stories of theft, violence and abandonment show that kinship with animals is far messier than environmental rhetoric admits, while offering a way to live with relationships that are painful or lost.
